news.title: Lettuce probe into largest foodborne illness outbreak of parasite in US history: Mexico's Health Ministry investigation finds shocking results
news.text:
ReutersFarm workers seen through shimmering heat while working on a lettuce farm near Salinas, California, U.S. (Reuters photo)

Mexico's Health Ministry said on Saturday that a US Food and Drug Administration investigation into the cyclospora parasite outbreak linked to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms in Mexico did not conclusively identify the source of contamination. Mexico's food-safety regulator Cofepris said tests conducted by its national reference laboratory on raw materials, finished products and water from the facility investigated in the outbreak were negative for the cyclospora parasite.The regulator added that environmental findings alone do not constitute conclusive evidence that agricultural products were the source of contamination. The FDA said on Friday it found a strong epidemiological and traceback link between the outbreak and recalled shredded iceberg lettuce produced by Taylor Farms in Mexico, but said there was insufficient evidence to determine how contamination occurred.The agency reported two environmental samples positive for cyclospora in Mexico, one from wastewater leaving a processing facility and another from a drainage ditch at an iceberg lettuce farm. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention declared the outbreak over on September 11. The outbreak sickened 12,883 people in 21 states, hospitalized 570 and was linked to two deaths.Mexico said it cooperated throughout the investigation, providing traceability information, inspections and samples, and would continue technical cooperation with US health authorities.The Food and Drug Administration said on Friday that its inspectors detected cyclospora at the Mexican farm blamed for the largest foodborne illness outbreak of the parasite in U.S. history.Live EventsYou Might Also Like:Daylight Saving Time: Donald Trump makes cell phone number of Republican Senator public over Sunshine Protection Act. What is the debate all about?Despite the finding, the FDA said it’s unclear how the parasite got into lettuce at Taylor Farms’ facility. The agency has now closed its investigation into the outbreak, which led to nearly 13,000 cases of diarrhea and other illnesses across the U.S.The announcement comes more than six weeks after the agency sent its investigators to the farm in Guanajuato, Mexico. The visit was the agency’s first time there in more than seven years following a steep drop in international food safety inspections after the COVID-19 pandemic.FDA inspectors said Friday they found cyclospora in two places: a wastewater tank and a drainage ditch used for lettuce cultivation. While it’s unclear how the contamination took place, the FDA said the samples provide “strong epidemiological data” linking the outbreak to the Taylor Farms site.Cyclospora is a microscopic parasite that commonly causes watery diarrhea “with frequent and sometimes explosive bowel movements,” according to the CDC. The illness, called cyclosporiasis, is less common than foodborne illnesses caused by other germs, including salmonella and E. coli.You Might Also Like:Tony Romo net worth, total fortune, annual salary: All about Ex-CBS analyst, legendary Dallas Cowboys quarterback wealthThe parasite is spread through human feces, and it still isn’t clear how sewage could have contaminated enough food to sicken so many people.Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now!

news.title: Former Bengals star Joe Mixon teases NFL comeback... just months after 'telling teammates his career is OVER' due to mysterious 'freak' condition
news.text:
Former Bengals star Joe Mixon teases NFL comeback... just months after 'telling teammates his career is OVER' due to mysterious 'freak' condition

MORE: Tony Romo's plans after quitting CBS Sports revealed by insiders

By DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 23:03 BST, 3 October 2026 | Updated: 23:03 BST, 3 October 2026

Former Cincinnati Bengals and Houston Texans star Joe Mixon has dropped a huge hint that he could make a return to the NFL.

The 30-year-old running back, who missed the 2025 season through a mystery injury, was released by the Texans in March. 

Houston general manager Nick Caserio had previously said Mixon was sidelined by a 'freak' foot injury. Then, in July, reports emerged that the running back had told some teammates that 'he is not going to play football anymore.'

KPRC-2 Houston said Mixon had been dealing with issues surrounding blood flow to his injured foot, on which he 'recently' underwent another surgery.

On Saturday, however, Mixon posted a video to social media which includes clips from his career and footage of him on the practice field.

The soundtrack to the video, meanwhile, features people questioning what had happened to Mixon and whether the running back would ever play again. 

😤⌛️@ononesock pic.twitter.com/seJczjDUuz
— ⚡️Primetime!!!⚡️ (@Joe_MainMixon) October 3, 2026

Former Bengals and Texans star Joe Mixon has hinted that he could make a return to the NFL

The running back, who missed last season through injury, was released by the Texans in March

Toward the end of the video, Mixon runs into the end zone during a practice session before shouting: 'Let's go! I'm back baby!' Alongside the footage, Mixon posted an hourglass emoji.

That was enough to convince many fans that a NFL comeback is on the horizon. But earlier this week, the 30-year-old launched a new company, ONE SOCK, which promises 'Better balance. More power. Faster recovery.' And Mixon's latest social media video ends with the ONE SOCK logo.

Without the two-time Pro Bowl selection, the Texans are 0-3 heading into week 4 of the new NFL season.

Houston provided few details on Mixon's recovery last season after announcing in training camp that he had sustained a foot injury away from the facility. 

It was only announced that the running back would miss 'an extended period of time'. In January, head coach DeMeco Ryans had no further update on Mixon's condition when asked if he will play next season.

'I don't know the answer to that right now,' Ryans told reporters. 'No clarity.'

Ryans also refused to shed any further light on the injury that kept the running back on the non-football injury list throughout 2025.

'He didn't jump off a building,' the coach said. 'He wasn't doing anything irresponsible. It was a freak thing.'

Houston TexansCincinnati Bengals
news.summary: The 30-year-old running back, who missed the 2025 season through a mystery injury, was released by the Texans in March.

news.title: "Unpredictability and unreliability": The real reason behind Tony Romo’s CBS exit? Network reportedly wanted freedom from $180M deal before arrest
news.text: Tony Romo’s nine-year run with CBS Sports is over, but the latest reporting suggests his July OWI arrest was not the full story behind the split. CBS and Romo announced Friday that they had mutually agreed to part ways, ending his time as the network’s lead NFL analyst. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback had four years and about $72 million left on the 10-year, $180 million deal he signed in 2020. According to The Athletic’s Andrew Marchand, CBS had concerns about Romo’s work and reliability before the arrest. The legal trouble, his reporting suggests, gave the network a reason to finally make a change.Why did CBS reportedly want out of Tony Romo’s contract?Marchand’s reporting points to problems that went beyond what happened in Milwaukee. He wrote that CBS wanted to “break free” of Romo’s contract because of concerns about his “unpredictability, lack of preparation, and unreliability.” His sources also told him Romo “didn’t work hard enough as a broadcaster” and “the further he got away from playing, the less he knew. He didn’t study and failed to learn new players and schemes.”Those are reported criticisms, not findings from CBS itself. Still, they add context to a relationship that had already become more complicated after Romo’s fast start in the booth.Romo joined CBS immediately after retiring from the NFL in 2017 and quickly built a reputation for predicting plays before they happened. That success helped lead to the huge 2020 extension. But according to Marchand, CBS executives had already discussed Romo’s broadcasting work with him before Super Bowl LVIII in 2024.That detail matters because it places the network’s concerns well before the July 2026 arrest.Did Tony Romo’s arrest give CBS a way out?Romo was arrested on July 23 in Wisconsin for operating a vehicle while intoxicated. He later pleaded no contest to the OWI charge and received a six-month driving suspension and a fine. CBS placed him on leave, with J.J. Watt moving into the lead booth alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson.The arrangement has now become permanent. CBS confirmed that Watt will continue as the network’s lead NFL analyst for the remainder of the season.Marchand put the situation bluntly: “The arrest was not the reason; it was the excuse.” He also reported that the settlement covering the final four seasons and $72 million of Romo’s contract came because CBS wanted to move on.The exact financial terms of that settlement have not been disclosed. What is clear is that CBS chose to end a contract that still carried a major financial commitment. Romo’s departure therefore appears to have been about more than one night in Milwaukee. The arrest changed the circumstances, but the reporting suggests the network had been questioning the relationship for some time.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. news.title: Larry Nassar controversy takes fresh twist as police dispute claim Team USA gymnastics doctor was removed from Michigan sex offender registry
news.text:
Larry Nassar controversy takes fresh twist as police dispute claim Team USA gymnastics doctor was removed from Michigan sex offender registry

READ MORE: Tony Romo's plans after quitting CBS amid claims of wake-up call

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and RICH JONES, US DEPUTY SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 22:27 BST, 3 October 2026 | Updated: 22:35 BST, 3 October 2026

Disgraced Team USA gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar was never on Michigan's sex offender registry, it has emerged. 

It was reported earlier this week that Nassar, who served as team doctor for the national gymnastics team from 1996 to 2014, had been quietly removed from the state's registry. 

However, Michigan State Police have now disputed that claim, revealing that the serial sexual abuser was not on the list in the first place.

'Information suggesting that convicted sex offender Nassar was removed from the Sex Offender Registry (SOR) by the Michigan State Police (MSP) because of the Smith decision is incorrect,' Lori Dougovito, a spokeswoman for Michigan State Police, told The Daily Mail in a statement.

In Michigan, only sex offenders living in the state are required to comply with and appear on its sex offender registry. 

'Offenders not currently domiciled, temporarily residing, working, incarcerated, or going to school in Michigan do not have the duty to register in Michigan under Michigan’s Sex Offender Registry Act (SORA), and would not be visible on Michigan’s public Sex Offender Registry (SOR),' Dougovito added. 

Michigan State Police have disputed a report that disgraced Team USA gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar (pictured) was removed from the state's sex offender registry 

Nasser is serving decades in prison after being convicted of multiple crimes 

'Should the offender later domicile (including being incarcerated), temporarily reside, work, or go to school in Michigan, they would be expected to register and be placed on Michigan’s public SOR if still required under SORA at that time.' 

Nassar is currently being housed at FCI Lewisburg in Pennsylvania. He has served time in federal, out-of-state prisons since pleading guilty in 2017. 

Should he return to a prison in Michigan, Nassar will then be entered onto the state's sex offender registry, police confirmed. 

Nassar, a former Michigan State University and USA Gymnastics doctor, used his position to exploit hundreds of young athletes, including medal-winning Olympic gymnasts Simone Biles and Aly Raisman.

He is currently serving multiple prison sentences lasting decades after being convicted on multiple counts of sexual abuse and child pornography in both federal and state court.

Nassar's federal conviction in 2017 on child pornography charges carried a 60-year sentence. Should he survive to serve the full sentence, he will then be required to serve 40 to 175 years in Michigan prisons on seven state-level sexual assault charges in Ingham County. 

He also faces a 40-year to 125-year prison sentence in Eaton County on additional sexual assault charges.

Speculation that he had been removed from Michigan's sex offender registry began earlier this week following a social media announcement from the Eaton County (Michigan) Prosecutor's Office. 

 Nassar is pictured in court during his sentencing hearing in Michigan in January 2018

Nassar, a former Michigan State University and USA Gymnastics doctor, used his position to exploit hundreds of young athletes, including Team USA gymnasts 

The post claimed that the 63-year-old Nassar was among more than 20,000 people whose names have been removed from the sex offender list after the Michigan State Police recently purged thousands of individuals from the database whose crimes happened before July 1, 2011. 

A Michigan Supreme Court ruling on September 9 said that amendments to the Sex Offender Registration Act issued in 2021 cannot be used to retroactively require registration due to older incidents, leading to the purge of the database.

The prosecutor's office wrote on social media that: 'The Michigan Supreme Court's decision to eliminate SORA requirements for these offenders is deeply concerning. Our community, along with the victims of these crimes, expected the registry to provide a measure of protection and awareness - assurances that have now been removed by the Court's ruling.'

The registry is intended to 'assist the public' with preventing future criminal sexual acts by convicted sex offenders, according to Michigan State Police, and typically lists a legal name, photo, primary address, work address, age, physical description and court with records relevant to the criminal conviction. 

The Eaton County Prosecutor's Office issued a statement on Friday, correcting its original post. 

'We must correct our earlier social media post about removal of convicted sex offenders from the Michigan Sex Offender Registry,' it wrote. 'After reporting from the Detroit News, it appears that Larry Nassar was never actually registered under the Michigan Sex Offender Registry. 

'We never contemplated that one of the most notorious sex offenders in the history of the state would not have been registered despite the law requiring otherwise. In our experience, when a sex offender is sentenced to a term of incarceration, they are listed in the Michigan Sex Offender Registry as being “incarcerated” and complaint (sic). That status does not change until the offender is released from custody, at which time the entity incarcerating the individual ensures the registry is updated.'

More than 150 gymnasts were abused by Nassar during his 30-year career. Nassar admitted to sexually assaulting the athletes when he worked at Michigan State University and USA Gymnastics.

Olympic icon Simone Biles was among Nasser's long list of hundreds of victims

The doctor also admitted to possessing child pornography, and more than 100 women sought over $1billion from the federal government for the FBI's failure to stop him. 

He was sentenced in federal court in 2017 to 60 years in prison on charges of possessing child sex abuse material. The following year, Nassar was sentenced to up to 175 years and up to 125 years, respectively, in two separate Michigan courts for molesting female gymnasts under his care.

Following the federal sentencing, U.S. Attorney Birge said: 'Today was a day of reckoning for Larry Nassar. He more than deserves this punishment for what he did.

'He consumed child pornography on a massive scale. We found 37,000 images of child pornography on his computers. Insatiable hunger of that nature simply encourages those who produce such images to continue to sexually exploit children. Compounding his danger to the public, 

'Nassar was an insidious hands-on child predator in his own right. He took advantage of family friendships. And he treated his license to practice medicine as a license to sexually molest children. Thanks to the brave victims who came forward, we learned the full scope of his depravity. The breadth and dark depth of his heinous acts are extraordinary.'

In April 2024, the US Justice Department announced a $138.7 million settlement with more than 100 people who accused the FBI of grossly mishandling allegations of sexual assault against Nassar in 2015 and 2016, a critical time gap that allowed the sports doctor to continue to prey on victims before his arrest.

When combined with other settlements, $1billion now has been set aside by various organizations to compensate hundreds of women who said Nassar assaulted them under the guise of treatment for sports injuries. 

Simone Biles publicly broke her silence in January 2018, revealing in a powerful tweet that she was one of Nassar's victims.

'It took me a long time to write that, probably a couple of days, because every time I would go to write, I would start bawling, and I couldn't get through it,' she said.

Biles also noted that she was heartbroken over having to continue to train at the ranch, the former USA Gymnastics national training center where she and her teammates were abused by the disgraced doctor.

Team USASimone Biles
news.summary: It was reported earlier this week that Larry Nassar, who served as team doctor for the national gymnastics team from 1996 to 2014, had been quietly removed from Michigan's sex offender registry.
news.author: Editor,Isabel Baldwin,Rich Jones

news.title: Kate Upton takes brutal MLB dig after crying during Justin Verlander's final game
news.text:
Kate Upton couldn’t help but take a playful dig at America's pastime after her husband, Justin Verlander, played his final MLB game.

On Sept. 26, Verlander — who was hilariously called out for using Upton’s Zoom account last June — took the major-league mound one last time during the Detroit Tigers’ 4-3 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates. Back in July, the veteran pitcher announced that the 2026 campaign would be his final MLB season, bringing a storybook ending to his 21-year career.

During an appearance on ‘TODAY’ alongside Verlander, Upton did little to hide her excitement now that she is no longer obligated to watch baseball. It comes after a lip reader exposed Caitlin Clark's 8-word comment to a ref after an explosive altercation.

• Fed-up Aaron Rodgers completely ignores Steelers teammate in awkward sideline moment

• Tony Romo's day only gets worse just hours after $72M CBS exit confirmed

“I'm so excited,” the supermodel quipped when asked how she felt about her partner’s retirement. “I am never watching another baseball game again.” 

As the panel erupted into a fit of laughter, Upton added: “It was tears of joy for me.”

While stopping by the ‘Good Morning America’ studio, Verlander shed light on his emotional departure from last Saturday’s game. “There was so much emotion all weekend,” he told co-anchor Michael Strahan. 

“Obviously, your life as you know it is coming to an end, and I feel like I ran my race and gave everything I had to the game.”

Upon being pulled in the top of the sixth inning, Verlander was greeted by his seven-year-old daughter, Genevieve, who jogged onto the field and warmly embraced her father as Tigers fans rained down cheers at Comerica Park.

With Upton struggling to hold back tears nearby, Verlander proceeded to whisper several words in Genevieve’s ear before saying goodbye to his teammates and manager, A.J. Hinch. 

“I just wanted to make sure she knew that I was in a good place and I'm so happy she was out there with me,” Verlander explained when asked what he told Genevieve during the heartwarming moment.

• Urban Meyer calls for ban after crude celebration in front of Donald Trump

• Pat McAfee tells fans to 'rot' after Jason Kelce forced to apologize on ESPN

“So I whispered in her ear, ‘I'm just so happy.’”

Verlander achieved no shortage of success over his decorated career in the majors, amassing 266 wins en route to being named a 10-time All-Star and three-time Cy Young Award winner.

Despite coming agonizingly short of 300 wins, Verlander asserted that he harbors no regrets about how his time in the big leagues played out. “I think it's all how you look at it, right? I could be sad for what maybe I didn't do. I didn't make 300 wins. That was a goal,” he said.

“I'm not going to go home and lay my head on my pillow tomorrow night, no matter how the game goes, and be like, I left something out there. I think that gives me some ease.”

As for what comes next, Verlander voiced his desire to “make up for lost time” with Upton, Genevieve and his one-year-old son, Bellamy.

“My family means the world to me,” he added. “And I'm just so happy that I get the opportunity to make up for lost time.”

It comes after a furious Spike Lee was restrained in a New York Yankees suite during an ugly confrontation with a fan.
news.author: Matthew Neschis

news.title: Controversial missed field goal call leaves college football fans split as different angles spark fierce debate
news.text:
Controversial missed field goal call leaves college football fans split as different angles spark fierce debate

READ MORE: Tony Romo's plans after quitting CBS amid claims of wake-up call 

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 21:15 BST, 3 October 2026 | Updated: 21:17 BST, 3 October 2026

The final moments of Virginia Tech's agonizing loss against Pitt ended in controversy on Friday night. 

The Hokies were narrowly defeated by the Panthers in a 35-33 loss, ending their unbeaten start to the season. 

However, kicker John Love had the chance to clinch a dramatic victory for Virginia Tech in the dying seconds of Friday's game.

With just :03 seconds remaining, the fifth-year kicker had a potential game-winning 36-yard field goal. 

Love and the Hokies fans inside Lane Stadium appeared to believe that he made it but the officials disagreed. 

The kick sailed higher than the goal posts' reach making it unclear to viewers if the ball just snuck inside the left post. 

Virginia Tech MISSES the game-winning field goal attempt pic.twitter.com/ieGZZHzsuV
— Bunch Formation (@BunchFormationP) October 3, 2026

Virginia Tech kick John Love had a potential game-winning 36-yard field goal on Friday

Officials ruled that the fifth-year kicker missed the attempt, sealing the Hokies' defeat to Pitt

The fans behind the goal immediately started cheering as Love and his teammates began to celebrate. 

However, the official below the posts instantly ruled the kick wide left. The field goal was chalked off as a miss, sealing Virginia Tech's losing fate. 

Love protested at the time but Hokies head coach James Franklin did not argue the call in his postgame news conference. 

According to NCAA rules, kicks above the goal post must be fully inside the post to be declared good. Kicks that go higher than the post are also not subject to replay review. 

There was no conclusive angle shown on the ESPN broadcast from underneath the uprights. Footage of the kick from the TV broadcast and other angles from fan-filmed clips left viewers divided on social media. 

Many argued that the kick appeared to be good with some even hitting out at the 'horrible officiating.'

'By every measure of 'good', it's there. Wild,' one college football fan wrote on X, as another added: 'It looked just inside as it went over!!!!'

'Looked good to me. WOW,' said a third as another asked, 'As a neutral, is that not good?!'

The attempt left fans split online as many argued that the kick looked good from certain angles

Hokies head coach James Franklin admitted that he was unsure if the kick was good or not

'No skin in this game, that looked like a made field goal,' insisted another. 

Meanwhile, one questioned: 'With all the technology in the game, why isn't there cameras on the ends of the goal posts looking straight up?' 

However, others disagreed, claiming that the officials had made the right call. 

'So you can all see better from TV than the official right under the goal post? Nah,' one user wrote, hitting back at fans arguing that Love made the kick. 

'NO GOOD!!!,' claimed a second, replying to a video filmed in the stands. 

'kinda looks good, but it would be interesting seeing it from the refs position of ground level, right underneath that goal post, to see if the ball hooked before or after crossing the 'imaginary' extended goal post,' another user said. 

Pittsburgh trailed 14-0, but scored 21 unanswered points at one point to come from behind and then held on, all despite losing starting quarterback Mason Heintschel to an injury on the fourth play of the second half. 

Virginia Tech quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer throws a pass during the second half

Virginia Tech controlled much of the first half, but the Hokies started unraveling when Cameron Lindsey's interception of Ethan Grunkemeyer led to a 22-yard touchdown pass from Heintschel to Cataurus Hicks with 31 seconds left in the half, cutting the Virginia Tech lead to 24-21.

That was the first of four turnovers for the Hokies, and the Panthers turned those into 14 points.

Hokies head coach Franklin admitted following the game that he was unsure if the kick was good or not. 

'To be honest with you, from my angle, I don't know,' Franklin told reporters. 'I think John Love is the best kicker in the country. I had so much confidence that that thing was going to go through. From my angle, I couldn't tell you one way or another... The end of the day, they said it didn't go through so everything else, doesn't really matter a whole lot
news.summary: Virginia Tech were narrowly defeated by Pitt in a 35-33 loss, ending their unbeaten start to the season. However, kicker John Love had the chance to clinch a dramatic victory for the Hokies.
news.author: Editor,Isabel Baldwin

news.title: Tony Romo's plans after quitting CBS... as insiders tell of wake-up call that drove NFL legend to step away from network and try something new
news.text:
Tony Romo is confident he will get a 'second chance' after leaving CBS Sports - but he might not choose to take it.

Romo has stepped away from his role vowing to 'focus on my health and my family' after he accepted a plea deal having been arrested for OWI in Milwaukee on July 23.

He blamed a 'dependance on pain medication' after multiple back surgeries left him with 'constant, debilitating pain' and said 'my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol.'

The 46-year-old was placed on leave indefinitely by CBS, who promoted No.2 analyst JJ Watt into Romo's role alongside Jim Nantz for the start of the new NFL season.

Romo has now stepped away from his $18million-a-year contract and left the network, sparking questions over his next move.

The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback moved into the broadcast boost in 2017 after he retired from playing but now sees his current plight as a 'wakeup call' as he plots his next move. 

A source close to Romo and CBS Sports told the Daily Mail: 'Tony has accepted it, though not the ideal scenario; he sees it as a wakeup call and a reason to get better. It is what needs to be done. To get healthy is now his mission. 

'He believes he will eventually get a second chance if he wants it, but he could also ride off into the sunset because he has enough money to not have to do anything ever again. 

'He's going to miss it, because he misses playing and commentating was his outlet, so now he just has to figure out what is next after he gets himself physically better.'

Romo was a massive hit when he first entered the booth but his popularity dwindled among viewers in recent years in the lead up to his arrest.

He signed a 10-year, $180 million contract with CBS in 2020 but the network could now look to 'spread money around' after deciding to 'set a precedent' by parting ways. 

The source continued: 'It just became too difficult to reason keeping Tony on as a commentator, because if they brought him back, which many wanted to happen, it would have left a bad taste in other's mouths if it looked like they were giving him preferential treatment.

'By parting ways, CBS has set a precedent, that you have to do the right thing. If you mess up, you're out. 

'CBS sees it as everyone's replaceable and now they can spread money around for others. They looked at the season so far, and their ratings are fine; it didn't hurt them one bit, letting him go.'

The network confirmed former Houston Texans defensive end Watt will continue alongside Nantz moving forwards. The news broke shortly after Romo had teed off in the third and final round of a Q-school golf tournament at the Club at Forest Ridge in Broken Arrow, Oklahoma. 

Romo told The Daily Mail through a spokesperson on Friday: 'I'm proud of what I accomplished at CBS Sports over the last nine years. I approached my role as a game analyst the way I've approached everything in my life – with a desire to win and be the best that I can be.

'I'm going to use this time to take a break, something I've never done before, and focus on my health and my family before moving on to my next opportunity.

'I am grateful for my time with CBS Sports and for the continued support of my family and friends, as well as the NFL community and fans.
news.summary: Tony Romo has parted ways with CBS Sports months after his arrest with the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback preparing for his next chapter.
news.author: Editor,Rich Jones,Russ Weakland

news.title: Pat McAfee's $1million College GameDay field goal contest turns farcical as Iowa student produces 'worst in history'
news.text:
Pat McAfee's $1million College GameDay field goal contest turns farcical as Iowa student produces 'worst in history'

READ MORE: Tony Romo's plans after quitting CBS amid claims of wake-up call

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 18:30 BST, 3 October 2026 | Updated: 18:42 BST, 3 October 2026

One Iowa student may have secured themselves the unfortunate title of the worst kicker in the history of College GameDay. 

Pat McAfee and co. brought the popular ESPN program to Iowa City, home of the Iowa Hawkeyes, this week. 

And, as is now tradition, the panel invited one lucky student to have the chance of winning $1million with McAfee's field goal kicking contest. 

Finley Banfig, an Iowa fan, was the student selected to join the series of recent winners. However, instead of hitting the jackpot, she was left humiliated. 

The kick only traveled a few yards in a brutal miss in front of former NFL punter McAfee and Kirk Herbstreit. 

The college freshman was allowed to save face with a second chance, which was a slight improvement on her first attempt but still missed the posts. 

THIS KICK IS FOR TWO MILLION DOLLARS

LET'S GO FINLEY

OH NO #CollegeGameDay https://t.co/EYS3YKvTW2 pic.twitter.com/nZ6PJQmLTS
— Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) October 3, 2026

An Iowa student produced the 'worst kick in College GameDay history' on Saturday

Pat McAfee and co. brought the popular ESPN program to Iowa City this week

The shockingly poor attempt left fans stunned on social media with many critical users going as far as to brand it the 'worst kick in College GameDay history.' 

'You could have offered $45 trillion to pay off the national debt and still been fine,' joked one. 

'Literally the worst ever first attempt,' claimed another. 

'They could’ve offered her $100 million and she wasn’t making it,' added a third. 

The missed attempt likely offered McAfee and ESPN relief after they were forced to pay out for three weeks in a row. 

Students at Ole Miss, Texas and Tennessee earned over $3.5million combined over the past three weeks.

Banfig didn't walk away empty-handed, however. Former Indianapolis Colts tight end and Iowa legend Dallas Clark attended the GameDay kick and ended up giving her a hand. 

Finley Banfig, an Iowa fan, shockingly missed her first attempt at the field goal contest 

Clark, who moved back to the state after retiring from the NFL in 2014, launched a 30-yard pass through the field goal uprights, which resulted in the massive Hawkeyes fan receiving $150,000 and another $150,000 going to the Iowa Children's Hospital.

The contest has been McAfee's signature

A former West Virginia Mountaineers punter who went on to the NFL's Indianapolis Colts, McAfee launched the 'Kicking is Easy' competition when he joined the ESPN GameDay crew in 2023. 

Remarkably, McAfee funded more than $6 million in prize and charity money connected to the contest over its first three seasons, but is now being matched by Home Depot, according to Front Office Sports.
news.summary: Finley Banfig, an Iowa fan, was the student selected to join the series of recent winners in Pat McAfee's College GameDay kicking contest. However, instead of hitting the jackpot, she was left humiliated.
news.author: Editor,Isabel Baldwin

news.title: Tony Romo and CBS Sports Part Ways After Nine Seasons in the NFL Booth
news.text:
Tony Romo and CBS Sports ended their nine-year broadcasting partnership on Friday, closing the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback’s tenure as the network’s lead NFL analyst after his arrest and no-contest plea in a Wisconsin operating-while-intoxicated case. CBS Sports said the decision was mutual and confirmed that J.J. Watt would remain with play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz and sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson on its top NFL crew for the rest of the 2026 season.

Romo said he would step away from work to focus on his health and family before considering another opportunity. The announcement resolved a question that had followed CBS since it placed him on indefinite leave during the summer.

Romo, 46, was arrested July 23 after a traffic stop in Milwaukee and later pleaded no contest to a first-offense civil OWI charge on September 1, according to The Associated Press. The plea resulted in a six-month loss of driving privileges and participation in an alcohol assessment program, AP reported. CBS had removed Romo from broadcasts after the arrest while it reviewed the matter, leaving Watt to work with Nantz and Wolfson. Friday’s statement converted that temporary change into the network’s plan for the balance of the season, while CBS said its other announcing teams would remain intact.

The separation followed a period in which Romo publicly accepted responsibility for the case and described a struggle with alcohol that he connected to chronic pain from his playing career. In his statement Friday, he said he was proud of his work at CBS and grateful for support from his family, friends, the NFL community and fans. He did not announce a timetable for returning to television or another public role. CBS likewise did not disclose financial terms or characterize the agreement beyond saying the two sides had mutually decided to part ways, leaving any contract settlement outside the verified public record.

Romo joined CBS immediately after retiring from the Cowboys in 2017 and moved directly into the network’s No. 1 NFL booth with Nantz, an unusually prominent assignment for a first-time game analyst. His early broadcasts drew attention for rapid diagnosis of formations and his willingness to forecast plays before the snap, a style that reflected the responsibilities he had carried as an NFL quarterback.

Over nine seasons he became one of the most recognizable voices in American sports television and worked major playoff games and Super Bowls. CBS’s decision therefore changes more than one weekly lineup: it ends a pairing that had become central to the network’s NFL presentation.

His playing record gave the move to television immediate credibility. NFL career statistics show that Romo spent his entire playing career with Dallas, while Pro Football Reference credits him with 34,183 passing yards in 156 games and four Pro Bowl selections. He rose from an undrafted free agent to the Cowboys’ starting quarterback, leading the team for most of a decade before injuries and the emergence of Dak Prescott brought his playing career to an end. That history allowed him to explain protection calls, coverage rotations and quarterback decisions from the perspective of a player who had managed them in real time.

CBS’s NFL business gives the personnel decision wider importance. The network is one of the league’s long-term media partners under agreements that run through the 2033 season, and the NFL’s distribution plan assigns CBS Super Bowls after the 2027 and 2031 seasons in addition to its regular Sunday package. Paramount’s agreement also extends NFL programming across CBS, Paramount+ and other platforms. The lead announcing team is therefore attached to one of the most valuable recurring products in television, and its members serve as both journalists and prominent representatives of the network’s sports brand.

The timing gave CBS a ready successor. Watt joined CBS Sports in 2023 after a 12-year NFL career and initially appeared on the studio program “The NFL Today.” He later moved into game coverage and had already been working beside Nantz during Romo’s leave.

CBS said Watt, Nantz and Wolfson would remain together for the rest of this season, avoiding a midseason search and preserving continuity for games assigned to the network’s top crew. The statement did not promise that the arrangement would extend beyond the current season, so longer-term decisions remain for CBS to make.

Watt brings a different playing perspective to the booth. He was a three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and recorded 114.5 sacks during a career with the Houston Texans and Arizona Cardinals, according to the league record cited by CBS. Where Romo typically interpreted the offense through the quarterback’s view, Watt can emphasize pass-rush plans, line play, defensive fronts and the methods used to disguise pressure. That change does not require the broadcast to abandon offensive analysis, but it alters the balance of expertise beside Nantz and gives CBS an opportunity to frame games from the defensive side.
news.summary:
Tony Romo and CBS Sports ended their nine-year broadcasting partnership on Friday, closing the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback’s tenure as the network’s lead NFL analyst after his arrest and no-contest plea in a Wisconsin operating-while-intoxicated case. news.title: CBS Sports, Tony Romo split months after drunk driving arrest
news.text:
CBS Sports and Tony Romo mutually parted ways today, about 10 weeks after the broadcaster’s arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

Romo, a former Dallas Cowboys quarterback who had been the network’s lead NFL analyst since 2017, pleaded no contest to the civil charge in a Wisconsin court on Sept. 1.

“CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways. We thank Tony for his contributions over the past nine years and wish him the best moving forward,” the company said in a statement today.

The statement added that J.J. Watt will continue to partner with play-by-play veteran Jim Nantz and sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson on its No. 1 broadcast team for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season.

“I’m proud of what I accomplished at CBS Sports over the last nine years,” Romo said in a statement. “I approached my role as a game analyst the way I’ve approached everything in my life — with a desire to win and be the best that I can be. I’m going to use this time to take a break, something I’ve never done before, and focus on my health and my family before moving on to my next opportunity. I am grateful for my time with CBS Sports and for the continued support of my family and friends, as well as the NFL community and fans.”

Romo, 46, was pulled over and arrested on July 23 after he left a golf course in Wisconsin, prompting CBS to place him on an indefinite leave.

After pleading no contest to the OWI charge last month, Romo issued a statement that said his football injuries indirectly led to an “over-reliance on alcohol.”

In his playing days, Romo suffered significant injuries to his back, as well as three broken collarbones. He missed 10 regular-season games in 2010 and 12 in 2015, and he appeared in just one game in his final season.

“Multiple back surgeries ended my career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain. That pain led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol,” Romo wrote in the statement posted to Instagram.
